q: How does a Navi Mumbai data centre calculate Scope 2 emissions per kW of IT load?
title: Data centre Scope 2 per kW of IT load
short: Multiply total facility electricity, which is IT load times PUE, by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25 for the location-based figure, then divide by average IT load in kW. Report a market-based figure separately for renewable power bought under open access or certificates.
audience: Colocation and enterprise data centres in Navi Mumbai and the Mumbai region

ol: Total facility kWh from the utility bill and any on-site generation.
IT load kWh from UPS or PDU metering, to calculate PUE.
Average IT load in kW for the period.

p: The location-based figure uses the grid factor. The market-based figure uses the factor of power you have contracted, such as green open access with its certificates, and the grid factor for the rest. Report both; customers asking for their share usually want the market-based figure.
Colocation customers want their share. Allocate facility emissions by their metered IT kWh, so cooling and losses follow their load through PUE.

example.title: Worked example: one month (illustrative inputs)
lines: IT energy: 1,500 kW x 720 hours = 1,080,000 kWh
Facility energy at PUE 1.45: 1,080,000 x 1.45 = 1,566,000 kWh
Per kW of IT load: 1,111.86 t / 1,500 = 0.741 t CO2 per kW for the month
example.note: Load and PUE are illustrative; use metered IT and facility energy.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
